title: Best Free ChatGPT Plugins: What Is Actually Free?
summary: Every ChatGPT plugin installs at no cost, because the directory has no price field. Ten plugins across ten jobs, with each free tier checked against the vendor.
body_markdown:
Every plugin in ChatGPT's directory installs at no cost, and no listing shows a price. What a plugin costs depends on the vendor account you connect to it, and the free plans behind those accounts come in five shapes. Some last as long as you like. Others run out after three uses. Below are ten plugins for ten jobs, with each free plan checked against the vendor's own pricing page or docs.


*Last verified: 7 November 2026.*


**Disclosure: Scrimba makes Explain Video Generator, one of the ten plugins below.**


## What Does "Free" Mean in ChatGPT's Plugin Directory?


In ChatGPT's plugin directory, free means the plugin costs nothing to install. The allowances, caps and licence terms all live in the vendor account behind it.


Open any listing and you get a title, a tagline, a description, example prompts, an **Install plugin** button and an Information block with Developer, Category, Website, Version and legal links. None of those fields is a price.


The search box makes the same point. Type *free* into the[directory](https://chatgpt.com/plugins?ref=scrimba.com) and you get Freeway Insurance, Freediver, Free2move and Crbonfree. The search matches the letters in plugin names, since there are no prices for it to match.


What OpenAI does control is which plugins you can reach at all. In[its own wording](https://chatgpt.com/features/plugins/?ref=scrimba.com) :


> Select plugins are available in all plans, including ChatGPT Free, Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, Edu, and ChatGPT for Teachers. Some plugins require a paid plan.


Your workspace adds two more conditions. Plugins are on by default for Business subscribers and off on Enterprise until an admin turns them on. OpenAI's[help center](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001256-plugins-in-chatgpt-and-codex?ref=scrimba.com) adds that using one "depends on your plan, workspace, role, region, and its included capabilities".


One thing catches people at step zero. A plugin does nothing until you install it, and @ mentioning one you haven't installed returns ordinary text with no error. Install first, then judge the free plan, and read the vendor's pricing page instead of the listing.


## What Is Actually Free, by Job


Free plans vary a lot even between plugins in the same directory section, so the table is sorted by job. Every figure comes from the vendor's pricing page or docs, checked 7 November 2026.


Plugin, as listed Made by The job it does What the free plan gives you Where the limit bites first


GitHub OpenAI Read and triage a repository $0, unlimited public and private repos 2,000 CI/CD minutes a month


Trello Trello Run boards and cards 10 boards, 10 collaborators per Workspace Trello's AI features need a paid plan


Supabase Supabase Query and manage a database $0, 500 MB database, 50,000 monthly active users Paused after 1 week idle, 2 active projects


Vercel Vercel Labs Build and deploy web apps Hobby, $0, with usage caps Personal, non-commercial use only


Canva Canva Create and edit designs Free, 5 GB storage, 1.6M+ templates Up to 20 Standard or Premium AI uses a month


Figma Figma Design files and design to code Starter, free, unlimited drafts 20 MCP server tool calls a month


Notion Notion Docs, tasks and databases Free, for one person's projects 5 MB uploads, Notion AI is a trial


Zoom Zoom Recap and search meetings Basic, free, 100 participants Summaries for 3 hosted meetings a month


Spotify Spotify Find music, podcasts, audiobooks Search and playback for everyone Playlist from a description needs Premium


Explain Video Generator Scrimba AS Explain something as a narrated video Free to start: 1 explainer without an account, 5 on a free account The 5 never renew; video download is a Pro feature


## Free Plans That Cap How Much You Can Hold


These are the safest free plans in the directory. The plan is permanent, nothing is metered per prompt, and the ceiling is how much you store.


**GitHub** , listed as "Triage PRs, issues, CI, and publish flows" and built by OpenAI itself, starts from the strongest position. Its[pricing page](https://github.com/pricing?ref=scrimba.com) puts Free at $0 with unlimited public and private repositories, 2,000 CI/CD minutes a month and 500 MB of Packages storage.


The plugin reads repository files, folder structure and commit history. None of that touches the metered part of the plan, so for reading a codebase inside a chat the free plan covers everything you need. Scrimba's guide to[understanding a new codebase fast](https://scrimba.com/articles/how-to-understand-a-new-codebase-fast-2026/) covers what to ask once you are in.


**Trello** caps collaboration.[Its pricing](https://trello.com/pricing?ref=scrimba.com) gives Free up to 10 boards per Workspace, up to 10 collaborators and unlimited Power-Ups per board. Trello's AI features start at $5 a month. The plugin gives you another way into the same boards, and it can only create what your plan allows.


**Supabase** , listed as "Manage and query databases", puts its limit in one sentence on the[pricing page](https://supabase.com/pricing?ref=scrimba.com) : "Free projects are paused after 1 week of inactivity. Limit of 2 active projects." A paused project still exists, but a plugin can't query it until you restore it. Underneath runs the same[Model Context Protocol](https://scrimba.com/articles/best-mcp-servers-for-developers-2026/) plumbing as most of these plugins.


## Free Plans That Cap the AI


Here the free plan is permanent and generous on storage. What it meters is the exact thing you installed the plugin to do.


**Canva** , listed as "Create, review, edit designs", gives a lot away:[its pricing](https://www.canva.com/pricing/?ref=scrimba.com) lists more than 1.6 million templates and 5 GB of cloud storage on Free. The AI allowance is small and shrinking. The pricing card now says only "Limited access to Standard and Premium AI". The FAQ further down the same page puts Free at up to 20 uses of Standard or Premium AI tools a month, one pool that resets monthly. Earlier this year it was up to 200 Standard or 20 Premium uses, and[PricingSaaS](https://pricingsaas.com/news/article/canva-hides-free-plan-s-ai-quota-behind-vague-wording?ref=scrimba.com) dates the cut to September 2026. Twenty generations is about one afternoon spent on a single poster.


Canva also names a paid requirement on the listing itself, which almost no other vendor does. Its[directory entry](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_connector_68df33b1a2d081918778431a9cfca8ba?ref=scrimba.com) says "Bulk Create requires an eligible Canva Enterprise plan", so one of its advertised skills is closed to every plan below Enterprise.


**Figma** is free on its Starter plan with unlimited drafts and, per[its pricing](https://www.figma.com/pricing/?ref=scrimba.com) , 150 AI credits a day up to 500 a month. The row that decides whether the plugin is usable sits in Figma's[developer docs](https://developers.figma.com/docs/figma-mcp-server/rate-limits-access/?ref=scrimba.com) . The MCP server, the layer that lets AI tools read your Figma files, allows **up to 20 tool calls a month** on Starter. A Full or Dev seat on Professional gets up to 200 a day. One conversation that reads a file, lists its components and exports a frame can use three.


**Notion** is direct about who its free plan is for.[Its pricing](https://www.notion.com/pricing?ref=scrimba.com) describes Free as "For individuals to organize personal projects and life", with uploads capped at 5 MB per file. Notion AI on Free is a trial: the[help center](https://www.notion.com/help/notion-ai-faqs?ref=scrimba.com) says Free and Plus users "get a limited number of complimentary AI responses so they can try Notion AI features out". You keep the workspace. The AI runs out.


## Free Plans That Cap Who You Are, or What the Plugin Is For


Two more shapes, and both break an assumption people bring to a free plan.


The first is a licence cap, and **Vercel** shows it plainly. Its plugin sits under Developer Tools with the example prompt "@Vercel why is my build failing?". The Hobby plan costs nothing, and Vercel's[Hobby docs](https://vercel.com/docs/plans/hobby?ref=scrimba.com) state the condition in one line.


So Hobby is a separate licence, and it ends where your project starts earning. Go over a usage limit and you wait out a 30-day pause. Use it for paid work and you need[Pro](https://vercel.com/pricing?ref=scrimba.com) , however little you deploy.


The second shape hurts more: the plugin's headline job is the part the free plan leaves out.


**Zoom** 's plugin is built around recapping and searching meetings. On[Zoom's pricing page](https://zoom.us/pricing?ref=scrimba.com) , Basic is free with up to 100 participants, but meetings run 40 minutes against 30 hours on Pro. Meeting summaries cover three hosted meetings a month, and Pro makes them unlimited. A plugin whose job is recapping meetings runs out after three recaps.


**Spotify** draws the line more precisely. Asking for songs, artists, genres, playlists, podcasts and audiobooks works for anyone. Its[listing](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_68de829bf7648191acd70a907364c67c?ref=scrimba.com) names the exception in its own words: "Spotify Premium listeners can describe a vibe and get a playlist made to match."[Premium Individual](https://www.spotify.com/us/premium/?ref=scrimba.com) is $12.99 a month after the trial. Most people install this plugin to describe a mood and get a playlist back, and that part costs money.


Three checks catch a job cap before you connect anything:


- Read the plugin's example prompts, then find the matching row in the vendor's pricing table. A blank free column means the demo is a paid feature.
- Look for a monthly count on the plugin's core action. "3 meeting summaries" limits the job itself; "5 GB of storage" only limits how much you keep.
- Check whether the plan limits *who* may use it. A personal-use clause appears in no allowance.


## Free to Start: A Fixed Allowance


The fifth shape is a starting allowance: a fixed number of uses for the life of the account. It is generous on day one and never resets, unlike the monthly AI allowances above.


**Scrimba Explain** , listed as *Explain Video Generator* under Education & Research, works this way. Its developer is Scrimba AS. It turns a topic, document, webpage, codebase or product brief into a narrated video with voiceover, diagrams, animations and code walkthroughs. You can make one with only the plugin installed; keeping more takes a free Scrimba account.


Scrimba's[docs](https://docs.scrimba.com/explain/limits-and-plans?ref=scrimba.com) publish the terms. Without an account you get one free explainer. A free account gets five, "a one-off allowance for the life of the account, not a monthly one, so it doesn't renew". Pro raises that to 100 a month.


A free account also gets three edits per explainer. Downloading an explainer as a video file, switching off the watermark and commercial use are all Pro features. Next to Canva's 20 AI uses a month or Figma's 20 tool calls, five lifetime explainers will show you what the tool does, but they won't carry a weekly habit.


Explain has no avatars, stock footage or brand templates, so it won't replace a marketing video tool. It explains one thing at a time, a narrower job than "video generator" suggests. Scrimba's own FAQ says it can make mistakes, so check anything that matters.


[scrimba.com/explain](https://scrimba.com/explain?ref=scrimba.com) has a public gallery of published explanations you can browse without an account. Scrimba's[guide to using Explain](https://scrimba.com/articles/how-to-use-scrimba-explain/) covers what makes a good prompt. If you want to produce videos in general, the[roundup of video plugins](https://scrimba.com/articles/best-chatgpt-plugins-for-creating-videos-2026/) ranks that category.


## How to Check a Plugin's Free Plan in Two Minutes


Two minutes of checking saves an afternoon spent hitting a cap. Start at the listing and work outward, because the hardest limits sit furthest from it.


1. **Read the listing's Information block and requirements.** Most listings name no plan. When one does, as Canva's Enterprise line does, that is the hardest limit you will find.
2. **Open the vendor's pricing page.** Homepages advertise the free plan. Pricing pages define it, usually below the plan cards.
3. **Find the row that matches your job.** "Free" and "3 meeting summaries a month" can sit in the same column.
4. **Look for the three limits that stop work:** a metered allowance that resets, a licence clause on who may use it, and an inactivity rule that pauses things while you are away.
5. **Check your own ChatGPT plan and workspace last.** Some plugins require a paid plan, and Enterprise workspaces keep them off until an admin enables them.


Then pick the shape of free that matches how you work, and only then the plugin. A weekly repository reader and a commercial site get opposite answers on the same tool. Scrimba's[guide to installing a plugin in ChatGPT](https://scrimba.com/articles/how-to-install-a-plugin-in-chatgpt-2026/) walks through the install itself, and its audit of[free AI video generators](https://scrimba.com/articles/free-ai-video-generators-2026/) applies the same checks to one category.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Are ChatGPT plugins free?


Every plugin installs at no cost, and the directory shows no prices. What varies is the vendor account behind it, which may carry a permanent free plan, a metered monthly allowance, a licence limited to personal use, or a starting allowance that never renews. OpenAI states that some plugins need a paid ChatGPT plan.


### Does ChatGPT charge for plugins?


No. OpenAI states that select plugins are available on all plans including ChatGPT Free, though some require a paid plan. Storage, allowances and billing sit with the vendor you connect, so a ChatGPT subscription buys none of it. Enterprise workspaces keep plugins off until an admin enables them.


### Which ChatGPT plugins have the most generous free plans?


GitHub, Trello and Supabase publish permanent free plans that cap what you store, so nothing is metered per prompt. GitHub Free is $0 with unlimited public and private repositories, Trello Free covers 10 boards per Workspace, and Supabase Free allows two active projects.


### Why does the plugin directory not show prices?


A listing carries a title, tagline, description, example prompts, an install button and an Information block naming the developer, category and version. None of those is a price, because pricing belongs to the vendor's account. Searching the directory for free matches plugin names instead.


### What does "free to start" mean?


It means a starting allowance: a fixed number of uses that does not renew. Scrimba Explain gives 1 explainer without an account, 5 on a free account and 100 a month on Pro, so the free allowance is enough to judge the tool, and regular use needs Pro.


## Key Takeaways


- **The directory has no price field.** A listing shows the developer, category and version, never a price, so free is always a claim about the vendor.
- **Free plans come in five shapes:** capped by storage, by an AI allowance, by licence, on the plugin's own core job, or a starting allowance that never renews.
- **The job cap is the one that hurts.** Zoom's free plan covers summaries for three meetings a month; Spotify's playlist generation needs Premium.
- **AI allowances change.** Canva cut its free AI uses from up to 200 a month to up to 20 in September 2026.
- **Licence limits appear in no allowance.** Vercel's Hobby plan costs nothing and restricts you to personal, non-commercial use.
- **Free to start is a fixed allowance.** Scrimba Explain gives 1 explainer without an account, 5 on a free account and 100 a month on Pro, and the free five never renew.
- **Read the vendor's pricing page instead of the listing,** and find the row matching your job.
